reason: Independent review of Persona Character P0 V2 proved that generic delegated-governance authorization currently ignores later supersession declarations. The first authorization attempt for this repair, merged by PR #152, is intentionally treated as non-effective evidence because concurrent trusted-main advancement made its actual authorization merge first parent differ from the base.commit recorded in that authorization. This V2 work package re-authorizes only the same minimum policy/test root repair and adds no product, workflow, dependency, release, or production scope.

authorizationMergeTransport.required: Construct the final ordinary two-parent authorization merge commit only after reading the exact current trusted main. The merge commit first parent must be that exact current main and equal this document base.commit; the second parent must be the independently reviewed exact authorization Head. Update refs/heads/main only with a non-force fast-forward ref update. If trusted main advances before the ref update, the ref update must fail and the proposal must be refreshed and re-reviewed rather than creating mismatched authority.

targetDefect.requiredSemantics: When trusted main contains exactly one later valid delegated authorization that explicitly supersedes an earlier authorization/implementation branch identity, the earlier branch must not receive delegated implementation authority. Historical commits and refs remain immutable evidence; revocation is policy evaluation, not history rewrite.

mandatoryFailureFirstContracts: Before the policy repair, a fixture containing a valid V1 delegated authorization plus a later valid V2 authorization that explicitly supersedes V1 must demonstrate RED because product/v21-persona-character-p0-v1 is still accepted as an authorized implementation branch.
After the repair, the same V1 branch must fail closed while the V2 implementation branch remains eligible under the later authorization once that authorization is effective.

Supersession must be resolved only from authorization documents that are themselves valid, uniquely introduced by an ordinary two-parent trusted-main merge, and present on the evaluated trusted main; proposal-only or malformed documents must not revoke authority.

A supersession declaration must bind the superseded authorization path and implementation branch exactly; ambiguous, self-referential, cyclic, duplicate or mismatched supersession must fail closed rather than pick an authority heuristically.
Unrelated delegated work packages must retain their existing authorization behavior.
No wildcard branch/path authority, force-reset, branch deletion, history rewrite, workflow weakening, warning-only behavior or temporary bypass is permitted.
The implementation diff must contain exactly the two authorized paths and preserve all existing generic delegated-governance integrity checks unless a stricter fail-closed condition is added.
